title: Truly subquadratic preprocessing for stretch-3 distance oracles
formal: For every fixed \(\varepsilon\in(0,1]\), do there exist constants \(\delta>0\) and \(C\), and a uniform randomized preprocessing algorithm, such that every simple undirected nonnegatively weighted graph with \(n\) vertices and \(m\le n^{2-\varepsilon}\) edges can be turned in expected \(Cn^{2-\delta}\) time into a distance oracle using \(Cn^{3/2}\) cells and worst-case \(C\) query time, whose estimate satisfies \[d_G(u,v)\le D(u,v)\le3d_G(u,v)\] for every connected vertex pair? Constants may depend on \(\varepsilon\), but not on the graph, its weights or \(n\).
definitions:
The input is the explicit adjacency lists of a graph with labelled vertices \([n]\), no loops and at most one edge per unordered vertex pair. Edge weights are finite real numbers at least zero. The shortest-path distance is the minimum total edge weight on a path. The oracle returns infinity exactly for disconnected pairs and zero on the diagonal; the multiplicative bound also forces exact zero whenever distinct vertices have zero distance. There is no additive error term and no requirement to report a path.

Use a random-access arithmetic machine with one exact real per weight cell and \(\Theta(\log n)\)-bit words for identifiers and polynomial-size addresses. Addition, subtraction, multiplication, nonzero division, comparisons, word operations and a cell access have unit cost; arbitrary bit extraction from a real does not. Preprocessing must terminate almost surely and every output structure must be correct for every query. Expected preprocessing time is taken over internal random choices for each fixed input. This is a Las Vegas convention, with worst-case size and query time once construction finishes.

All retained copies of input data count toward oracle space. The input cannot be read from an uncharged external memory during a query. The bound is an operation count in this model, not a finite-precision bit-complexity claim. There is no coordinate or edge-weight magnitude dependence. A single finite program can accept the fixed density parameter; equivalently a uniform family indexed by fixed rational positive density slack is sufficient.

The exponent improvement \(\delta\) may shrink with \(\varepsilon\), but must be positive and independent of \(n\). Writing a density bound with an arbitrary fixed multiplicative constant gives the same existence question after decreasing the slack. For \(\varepsilon>1\), the input class is contained in the \(\varepsilon=1\) class, so the displayed range covers the original all-positive-slack target. The oracle is specifically stretch three, corresponding to \(k=2\) in the family of stretch \(2k-1\) tradeoffs.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of existence with the stated quantifier order and simultaneous construction, space and query guarantees, or its logical negation. A conditional lower bound must retain its assumption and does not alone refute the unconditional proposition. A result only for larger stretch, an additive-error guarantee, or a preprocessing bound of \(n^{2-o(1)}\) does not meet the fixed positive exponent saving.
context:
Kadria and Roditty formulate the subquadratic construction problem and obtain such preprocessing for every integer k greater than two. Their introduction explicitly leaves k=2, or stretch three, as the remaining case.

The source emphasizes that even an unweighted version without a small-space requirement would represent a significant advance. This card retains the stronger imported combination of weighted graphs, O(n^(3/2)) space and constant-time queries.
why: The remaining stretch-three case tests whether compact distance oracles can be built genuinely faster than quadratic time on sparse inputs.

import_provenance.original_title: Truly subquadratic preprocessing for stretch-3 distance oracles
import_provenance.original_statement: For every fixed epsilon > 0, can a nonnegatively weighted undirected graph with m=O(n^(2-epsilon)) edges be preprocessed in O(n^(2-delta)) time, for some delta > 0, into a stretch-3 oracle with O(n^(3/2)) space and constant query time? Kadria and Roditty's 2025 work settled the analogous preprocessing question for stretch 2k-1 when k>2, leaving k=2 open.

sentences: A sparse weighted graph is preprocessed into a structure answering approximate distance queries.
The required stretch is three, space is O(n^(3/2)) and query time is constant.
For every fixed subquadratic density, preprocessing must save a fixed positive power over quadratic time.
The checked 2025 paper achieves the analogous construction for larger stretch but leaves this case open.
The target isolates the low-stretch barrier in fast approximate graph-distance preprocessing.
